I’ve been farming these 20 mu for 35 years, since I was 15. My old man taught me, and I’ve seen good years, bad years, and everything in between. With 8 mouths at home and a couple of the younger ones working off-farm in Shijiazhuang, I can’t afford to gamble. I don’t have a university education, but I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets and do basic sums. Still, what I trust most is what I see with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

**Winter wheat** — I’ll plant around October 10th, same as always, on all 20 mu. I buy the improved Jinmai variety, about 40 yuan per mu. It sprouts reliably and the grain station takes it without complaints. I rotary-till after the maize comes off, then drill the seed. For fertilizer, the extension fellow says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but last year I tried that and the wheat looked a bit yellow at jointing, so this year I’m doing 17 kg nitrogen per mu. I put down compound fertilizer as base before planting — about 40 kg per mu — and then topdress with urea at jointing in March. I’ll irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well water isn’t free anymore with those meters, so three times is my limit. I spray herbicide in spring; the weeds get bad otherwise. I hire a combine for harvest — the window is too tight to do it by hand — and get my nephew to help with the turnover. I’m expecting about 420 kg per mu if spring cooperates.

**Summer maize** — This goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. I have maybe four days to get it planted or I lose yield. I use hybrid seed, about 50 yuan per mu. Two bags of compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at the big喇叭口 stage. Total nitrogen around 16 kg per mu. The maize needs less irrigation than wheat — twice should do it, at jointing and filling, unless the rains come good. I spray herbicide and maybe insecticide once if I see borers. Family handles most of the work, but I hire a couple of hands during the busy planting week. I’m hoping for 480 kg per mu.

Total spending this year will run about 17,200 yuan. That’s a lot of cash to lay out, but with grain prices what they are, I need the yield. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad year — my family has to eat.
